label: Start-of-copy timing unit: delimiter step for short sequences (L<=4), first copy-input step for long sequences (L>=7)
explanation: Fires almost only at the start of the copy phase (recall_idx 0 or 1 holds 98% of activation mass); which of the two steps depends on sequence length. For short sequences (L=3: 100% of delimiter steps; L=4: 66%) it fires on the <DEL> step itself, and is almost never active on the following step. For long sequences (L=9: 97%, L=8: 83%, L=7: 44% of steps) it fires on the first copy step (input = fed-back first original token, outputting token 1), and rarely on <DEL>, except L=9 where <DEL> also fires on about 33% of steps. Mid lengths L=5-6 barely fire. Magnitude is largest at the first copy step of L=8-9 sequences (about 69% of mass) and on <DEL> for L=3; the top examples are L=9 first-copy steps and L=3 delimiter steps. Small residual activity at t=1 in the original phase. Never fires at recall_idx >= 2 or at t >= 11. Token identity has only weak effects (first token d or 3 slightly higher). The two-regime length dependence makes this look like an absolute-time/phase interaction rather than one clean concept, so precision and recall are both around 0.75.
